title: Zero-Downtime Deduplication of 50 Million Records Under Live Write Load
realWorldScenario: Due to an idempotent webhook failure, duplicate payment records were inserted into `payments` for the same `order_id` and `transaction_ref`. You must delete all duplicate rows, keeping only the earliest record (`MIN(id)`), while thousands of concurrent orders continue inserting into the table.
questionStatement: Write a chunked batch deduplication script using keyset ranges that identifies duplicate rows in `payments` by `(order_id, transaction_ref)` and deletes duplicates in small transactions (e.g. 5,000 IDs per iteration) to prevent locking the table or generating unmanageable WAL volume.
starterCode:
-- Chunked batch deduplication
WITH duplicates_in_chunk AS (
    SELECT id
    FROM (
        SELECT 
            id,
            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
                PARTITION BY order_id, transaction_ref 
                ORDER BY id ASC
            ) AS rn
        FROM payments
        WHERE id BETWEEN 1 AND 5000
    ) ranked
    WHERE rn > 1
)
DELETE FROM payments
WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM duplicates_in_chunk)
RETURNING id;
expectedConcepts: Why monolithic DELETE fails in production (locks, WAL explosion, replication lag)
Chunked keyset pagination (id BETWEEN x AND y)
ROW_NUMBER() window partitioning for duplicate identification
Small batch transactions with sleep throttle
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY to prevent recurrence
hints: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY order_id, transaction_ref ORDER BY id) identifies duplicates when row_num > 1.
Why must the query be restricted to an ID range like WHERE id BETWEEN 1 AND 5000?
Concurrently create a UNIQUE index after cleanup.

testCases.description: Verify chunked duplicate deletion keeping lowest ID
